**Finding: deviation (medium, commercial) — § 7.2**

§ 7.2 imposes a reverse MFN on us: before engaging another provider, Juniper Ridge must disclose and match for Cobalt any more favourable commercial offer it receives. The direction is wrong — the playbook welcomes MFN pricing in the customer's favour but rejects open-ended obligations to extend the vendor any better third-party terms. It also contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

Redline (validated, ok:true): delete p0026 in full. No Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere in the document, so nothing in our favour is affected; § 12.3 is retained. Fallback if pushed: an MFN limited to a single defined product, 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
